definitions.explanation: Musical support played alongside a main melody, typically on piano or other instruments to support a vocalist or solo instrument.

examples.japanese: ピアノの{伴奏|ばんそう}で{歌|うた}を{歌|うた}った。
examples.english: I sang a song with piano accompaniment.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}が{伴奏|ばんそう}を{担当|たんとう}してくれた。
examples.english: She took care of the accompaniment for me.

examples.japanese: {合唱|がっしょう}コンクールの{伴奏|ばんそう}を{練習|れんしゅう}している。
examples.english: I'm practicing the accompaniment for the choir competition.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
{伴|ばん} (accompany) + {奏|そう} (play music)

VERB FORM:
・{伴奏|ばんそう}する (to accompany - musically)

RELATED VOCABULARY:
・{伴奏者|ばんそうしゃ} (accompanist)
・ピアノ{伴奏|ばんそう} (piano accompaniment)
・{無|む}{伴奏|ばんそう}/アカペラ (a cappella, unaccompanied)
・{自動|じどう}{伴奏|ばんそう} (auto-accompaniment - keyboard feature)

CONTEXTS:
Piano accompaniment ({伴奏|ばんそう}) is an important role in Japanese school music, especially for:
・{合唱|がっしょう}コンクール (choir competitions)
・{卒業式|そつぎょうしき} (graduation ceremonies)
・{音楽会|おんがくかい} (music recitals)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{伴奏|ばんそう}を{弾|ひ}く (to play the accompaniment)
・{伴奏|ばんそう}に{合|あ}わせる (to match the accompaniment)
・{伴奏|ばんそう}を{務|つと}める (to serve as accompanist)
・{伴奏|ばんそう}{付|つ}き (with accompaniment)
